section_summary: This section contains inquiries from American holders of Japanese government and corporate bonds, together with State Department replies about unpaid interest, claims against vested assets, and possible treatment in a future peace settlement. It also includes correspondence about mortgaged Japanese power plants designated for reparations, British bondholders, and a mistaken report that U.S. consulates were collecting Japanese bonds.

people.name: James C. Corliss
people.role: Assistant Chief, Division of Financial Affairs

people.name: A. N. Overby
people.role: Special Assistant to the Secretary of the Treasury

people.name: Peter S. Ioki
people.role: Recipient of a sample State Department letter

people.name: H. J. Gochenaur
people.role: Administrator of Anton M. Turgasen’s estate

people.name: Harding Cowan
people.role: Special Attorney, Foreign Funds Control Department

people.name: Nelson Stuart
people.role: Trust officer, National City Bank of New York

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Taiwan Electric Power bonds
subfiles.to: Assistant Secretary of State for Occupied Territories
subfiles.about: Hoseley asks about the value, unpaid interest, and principal repayment of Taiwan Electric Power bonds.
subfiles.summary: Hoseley seeks information about a bond due in 1957 and possible reimbursement of American holders.

subfiles.title: Claim notice concerning Japanese government bonds
subfiles.about: An estate administrator reports two Japanese government bonds and asks how to record a claim.
subfiles.summary: Leonard lists 1924 and 1930 external loan bonds and attached unpaid coupons.

subfiles.title: Interim reply to Clarence S. Leonard
subfiles.about: The Department sends its press release on claims against vested Japanese assets.
subfiles.summary: Corliss promises a fuller reply and encloses press release No. 395.

subfiles.title: Report of Tokyo Electric Light bond holding
subfiles.about: Blyth reports ownership, purchase details, and unpaid coupons for a Tokyo Electric Light bond.
subfiles.summary: She records a $1,000 bond bought in 1928 and notes contact with a proposed bondholders committee.

subfiles.title: Interim reply to A. J. Blyth
subfiles.about: The Department provides notice of the filing process for claims against vested Japanese assets.
subfiles.summary: Corliss encloses press release No. 395 and promises a detailed reply.

subfiles.title: Inquiry listing Tokyo Electric Light bonds
subfiles.about: Abe lists bond numbers and asks for news about their prospects.
subfiles.summary: The handwritten inquiry identifies ten Tokyo Electric Light bonds and seeks current information.

subfiles.title: Reply to Toraji Abe on Tokyo Electric Light bonds
subfiles.about: The Department explains its bondholder policy and suggests sources of assistance and claim information.
subfiles.summary: Corliss apologizes for delay, describes the Council’s role and the uncertainty of a peace settlement, and requests details for the Department’s records. He refers Abe to the Office of Alien Property about vested assets.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning W. H. Hatton’s Taiwan Electric Power bonds
subfiles.about: The Department records corrected bond information and outlines its position on Japanese dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: Corliss explains that the Department does not negotiate directly for holders, points to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and notes that peace settlement terms remain unknown. He suggests contacting the Office of Alien Property about a debt claim.

subfiles.title: Correction of Taiwan Electric Power bond identification
subfiles.about: Hatton corrects an earlier misidentification of his two bonds and requests help recovering payment.
subfiles.summary: He supplies bond numbers, terms, maturity, and the date of attached coupons.

subfiles.title: Routing slip to the Division of Financial Affairs
subfiles.from: Office of the Under Secretary for Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: An item is forwarded for appropriate action.
subfiles.summary: Internal routing slip forwarding material for action.

subfiles.title: Treasury referral of Frederick A. Lewis’s inquiry
subfiles.about: The Treasury forwards Lewis’s inquiry and bond list to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Overby encloses Lewis’s letter and a copy of Treasury’s acknowledgment.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment to Frederick A. Lewis
subfiles.about: Treasury tells Lewis that his foreign bond inquiry has been referred to State.
subfiles.summary: The acknowledgment redirects the inquiry to the Department of State.

subfiles.title: Frederick A. Lewis’s inquiry and bond schedule
subfiles.about: Lewis asks about prospects for four Japanese corporate bonds listed in an enclosure.
subfiles.summary: The list names Tokyo Electric Light, Oriental Development, and Great Consolidated Electric Power issues.

subfiles.title: Interim reply to Alex Goldman
subfiles.about: The Department sends notice of claims against assets of former Japanese ownership.
subfiles.summary: Corliss encloses press release No. 395 and promises a fuller response.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Imperial Japanese Government sterling bonds
subfiles.about: The Goldmans ask how to register sterling bonds held for safekeeping in London.
subfiles.summary: They note prior registration with Treasury’s Foreign Funds Control in 1943.

subfiles.title: Detailed reply to Frederick A. Lewis
subfiles.about: The Department explains its foreign bond policy, requests additional holding details, and describes vested asset claims.
subfiles.summary: Corliss distinguishes private obligations from government guaranteed ones, points to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and says peace terms are unknown. He asks for acquisition, interest, and citizenship details and urges filing eligible debt claims with the Office of Alien Property.

subfiles.title: Interim reply to John C. Watson
subfiles.about: The Department sends Watson notice about claims involving vested German, Japanese, and Hungarian assets.
subfiles.summary: Corliss encloses press release No. 395 and promises a detailed reply.

subfiles.title: Watson’s supplemental bond and citizenship details
subfiles.about: Watson supplies purchase, interest, and naturalization details for Japanese, Hungarian, and German securities.
subfiles.summary: He lists Japanese government, Toho Electric, and Ujigawa Electric bonds, Hungarian mortgage bonds, and German conversion securities, with acquisition details and unpaid coupons.

subfiles.title: Reply to Paul W. Fenton concerning coupons
subfiles.about: The Department advises Fenton to file a claim for unpaid Tokyo Electric Light coupons.
subfiles.summary: Corliss apologizes for delay and identifies the Office of Alien Property claims process.

subfiles.title: Correction of filing deadline sent to Fenton
subfiles.about: The Department corrects the claims deadline in its previous letter.
subfiles.summary: The filing deadline is June 1, not June 30, 1947.

subfiles.title: Interim reply to George H. Elliott
subfiles.about: The Department sends notice of claims against vested Japanese assets.
subfiles.summary: Corliss encloses press release No. 395 and promises a detailed reply.

subfiles.title: Elliott’s Oriental Development bond details
subfiles.about: Elliott identifies three inherited Oriental Development securities and their unpaid interest.
subfiles.summary: He supplies certificate numbers, estate history, and citizenship by birth.

subfiles.title: Dillon, Read & Co. on power company bonds and reparations
subfiles.about: The firm asks how American bondholders’ mortgage interests will be protected when Japanese power assets are removed for reparations.
subfiles.summary: The letter details Daido and Shinyetsu bond issues, government guarantees, successor obligations, wartime conversions, and purported mortgage cancellations. It identifies Osaka’s Azikawa plant as designated for removal and asks about protection of bondholders’ security and blocked interest funds.

subfiles.title: Instruction to American mission in London about Japanese bond claims
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, London
subfiles.about: State explains the scope of claims against vested assets and responds to the Embassy’s bondholder inquiry.
subfiles.summary: The instruction distinguishes claims against each debtor’s vested assets from claims against Japan generally, notes that debt claims chiefly concern matured obligations, and encloses a press release and sample reply.

subfiles.title: Transmittal slip for London airgram
subfiles.about: The London airgram is forwarded internally.
subfiles.summary: Internal slip routes the airgram to financial affairs.

subfiles.title: London airgram on British holders of Japanese sterling bonds
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports a parliamentary exchange and requests information about U.S. bondholder claims procedures.
subfiles.summary: The Chancellor says Japanese exports must first cover essential imports and occupation costs. The Embassy asks for guidance after reports of American preliminary claims circulated in London.

subfiles.title: Record copy replacement notice
subfiles.about: A white airgram copy replaces an unreturned yellow action copy.
subfiles.summary: Records office designates the attached airgram as the filing copy.

subfiles.title: London airgram on British holders of Japanese sterling bonds, record copy
subfiles.about: A duplicate copy records the British parliamentary exchange and the Embassy’s request for U.S. claims information.
subfiles.summary: This is a second, poorer OCR copy of the airgram on page 405.

subfiles.title: Interim reply to H. J. Gochenaur
subfiles.about: The Department sends the estate administrator its notice on claims against vested Japanese assets.
subfiles.summary: Corliss encloses press release No. 395 and promises a detailed reply.

subfiles.title: Estate inquiry about Japanese and Hungarian bonds
subfiles.about: Gochenaur asks how to protect an estate’s interests in Japanese government and Hungarian bonds.
subfiles.summary: He lists bonds and unpaid coupons held by the late Anton M. Turgasen.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Herbert K. Brown
subfiles.about: State records Brown’s Tokyo Electric Light holdings and encloses its debt claims notice.
subfiles.summary: The Department will retain Brown’s information for possible future use.

subfiles.title: Brown’s report of Tokyo Electric Light bonds
subfiles.about: Brown reports four Tokyo Electric Light bonds, their purchase, last interest payment, and citizenship.
subfiles.summary: He asks the Department to record the holdings and says he will watch for public announcements.

subfiles.title: Interim reply to Frank Y. Toribara
subfiles.about: State provides its vested asset claims notice following Toribara’s referral from Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Corliss encloses press release No. 395 and promises a detailed reply.

subfiles.title: Federal Reserve referral of Toribara’s letter
subfiles.about: The Federal Reserve forwards Toribara’s inquiry about Japanese bond claims.
subfiles.summary: Cowan encloses Toribara’s letter and the bank’s response.

subfiles.title: Federal Reserve acknowledgment to Toribara
subfiles.from: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
subfiles.about: The bank refers Toribara’s inquiry to the Department of State.
subfiles.summary: The reply directs further correspondence to State.

subfiles.title: Toribara’s inquiry about Japanese bond claims
subfiles.to: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Toribara requests claim procedures and information about recovery on Japanese bonds bought through U.S. banks.
subfiles.summary: He seeks instructions after referral from the Federal Reserve’s Seattle branch.

subfiles.title: Reply to General Brokerage Company
subfiles.about: State explains where to find claims information and refers trading questions to securities regulators.
subfiles.summary: Corliss encloses press release No. 395 and suggests contacting the SEC’s Los Angeles office about trading.

subfiles.title: Brokerage inquiry on Japanese bonds and trading
subfiles.about: A brokerage asks about debt claim forms, eligibility, deadlines, and possible resumption of trading.
subfiles.summary: The inquiry covers several Japanese government, municipal, and utility bonds held by clients.

subfiles.title: Fenton acknowledgment of claims advice
subfiles.about: Fenton says he has requested forms from the Office of Alien Property.
subfiles.summary: He intends to file a claim after receiving the forms.

subfiles.title: Report of one Tokyo Electric Light bond
subfiles.about: Miyoshi reports a $1,000 Tokyo Electric Light bond for the Department’s records.
subfiles.summary: The letter identifies the bond number, interest rate, and 1953 maturity.

subfiles.title: Detailed reply to Arthur Sato
subfiles.about: State explains its policy on Tokyo Electric Light bonds and asks for citizenship information.
subfiles.summary: Corliss refers Sato to the Office of Alien Property for vested asset claims and to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council. He says the future of coupons and peace treaty treatment remains uncertain and offers to record Sato’s holdings if he is an American citizen.

subfiles.title: Initial acknowledgment to Arthur Sato
subfiles.about: State acknowledges Sato’s inquiry and sends the debt claims press release.
subfiles.summary: A fuller reply is promised.

subfiles.title: Sato’s inquiry about unpaid dividends
subfiles.about: Sato asks how to claim amounts due on Tokyo Electric Light bonds.
subfiles.summary: He requests forms and other useful information.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Carl H. Schuster
subfiles.about: State agrees to record Schuster’s Oriental Development bond information.
subfiles.summary: Corliss confirms the information will be retained for possible consideration.

subfiles.title: Schuster’s transmittal of bond correspondence
subfiles.about: Schuster sends copies of bank and Alien Property correspondence for the Department’s records.
subfiles.summary: He asks State to retain the enclosures concerning his Oriental Development bonds.

subfiles.title: Schuster’s request for debt claim forms
subfiles.about: Schuster identifies two Oriental Development bonds and requests claim forms.
subfiles.summary: He describes purchase, unpaid coupons, and citizenship by birth, then asks for forms before the filing deadline.

subfiles.title: National City Bank circular to Oriental Development bondholders
subfiles.from: Nelson Stuart, National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: The bank alerts holders to vesting orders and the deadline for filing eligible debt claims.
subfiles.summary: It identifies two Oriental Development debenture issues, directs holders to the Office of Alien Property for forms, and recommends legal advice on filing.

subfiles.title: Excerpt from State Department bondholder guidance
subfiles.from: National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: An excerpt quotes State’s policy on assistance to American bondholders.
subfiles.summary: The excerpt says State will record holdings and announce relevant developments publicly.

subfiles.title: Detailed reply to Fumiye Inouye
subfiles.about: State addresses Inouye’s Tokyo Electric Light bonds and family yen deposits at Japanese banks.
subfiles.summary: Corliss apologizes for delay, outlines the Department’s bond policy and the Council’s role, and requests purchase, interest, and citizenship details. He refers Inouye to the Office of Alien Property concerning possible claims on bonds and deposits.

subfiles.title: Inouye’s list of bonds and family bank deposits
subfiles.about: Inouye reports four Tokyo Electric Light bonds and yen deposits held by family members.
subfiles.summary: The list names bond numbers and deposits at the Yokohama Specie Bank and Sumitomo Bank.

subfiles.title: Lewis’s supplemental purchase information
subfiles.about: Lewis supplies acquisition and last interest details for his Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: He says the bonds were bought on the open market in 1929 and 1930 and last paid interest in 1941.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Lewis’s additional details
subfiles.about: State acknowledges the additional Japanese bond information.
subfiles.summary: The Department will add Lewis’s information to its records.

subfiles.title: Record copy replacement notice for Vancouver airgram
subfiles.about: A white airgram copy replaces an unreturned yellow action copy.
subfiles.summary: Records office designates the attached airgram as the filing copy.

subfiles.title: Vancouver airgram about bonds delivered to consulate
subfiles.about: The consulate asks what to do with Japanese bonds received after a newspaper report.
subfiles.summary: A Japanese Canadian publication reportedly told holders to deliver bonds to U.S. representatives; the consulate received bonds denominated in francs.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Vancouver consulate on bond custody
subfiles.about: State instructs the consulate to decline bonds and direct American holders to write with their holding details.
subfiles.summary: The Department says no U.S. agency is collecting Japanese bonds and explains that the newspaper may have confused bonds with debt claim filings.

subfiles.title: Detailed reply to Helen Setar Shutack
subfiles.about: State explains policy on her Japanese government guaranteed Shinyetsu Electric Power bond.
subfiles.summary: Corliss points to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, says peace settlement provisions are unknown, and offers to record the holding if Shutack provides citizenship details. Further action, if needed, would be announced publicly.

subfiles.title: Shutack follow-up and enclosures
subfiles.about: Shutack reports that the Office of Alien Property found no vested Shinyetsu assets and asks State to address her bond inquiry.
subfiles.summary: The first continuation page appears before the letter’s opening page, and its text is duplicated after it. Shutack encloses her correspondence with the Office of Alien Property, which said it could not entertain a claim against Shinyetsu.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about a Japanese government external loan bond
subfiles.about: Campbell asks how to collect on a 1924 Imperial Japanese Government bond and unpaid coupons.
subfiles.summary: He gives the bond number and asks whether repayment was included in war reparations.

subfiles.title: Detailed reply to Demetrius A. Pappy
subfiles.about: State explains its policy on Japanese government bonds and describes possible debt claims against vested assets.
subfiles.summary: Corliss points to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, says peace treaty terms are unknown, and requests holding and citizenship details for State’s records. He identifies the Office of Alien Property claims process and the September 1947 filing deadline.
